label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They appear to be psychologically well-adjusted, with UCLA-8 loneliness scores well below typical thresholds, near-minimal depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9, and virtually negligible anxiety on the GAD-7. Their moderate daily screen time (1–3 hours) suggests balanced digital engagement rather than excessive or avoidant use.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78), indicating strong social connectedness
Near-floor depressive symptom levels (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.25), suggesting minimal mood disturbance
Extremely low anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.04), reflecting psychological calm and stability
Moderate screen time of 1–3 hours per day, consistent with purposeful rather than compulsive usage
Higher educational attainment (graduate or above), potentially associated with greater coping resources
tone: Calm, stable, and socially connected with minimal psychological distress

label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their loneliness scores, depression scores, and especially anxiety scores are all in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring psychological distress alongside heavy digital engagement. With 178 respondents in this cluster, it represents a substantial subgroup characterized by the convergence of advanced education, extensive screen time, and pronounced emotional vulnerability.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen/internet use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Displays notably high anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.15, the most pronounced indicator)
Engages in prolonged daily digital use (more than 5 hours)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggests compounding emotional distress
tone: Concerned and empathetic, acknowledging significant psychological burden within a high-achieving, digitally engaged demographic

label: Emotionally Resilient Moderate-Use Graduate Woman
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging 1.22, PHQ-9 depression scores at 0.82, and GAD-7 anxiety scores at 0.83—all well below clinical thresholds—these individuals demonstrate strong psychological well-being. They engage in moderate daily screen or online activity (1–3 hours) and are highly educated, suggesting a balanced lifestyle that supports mental health.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily online/screen use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of loneliness or social isolation
Maintains moderate and bounded daily screen or internet use (1–3 hours)
Represents a sizable and stable subgroup (n=339), suggesting a common well-adjusted pattern
